# VARMINTS — LADDER AND ROOF RUN: THEY RUN (14s)
Genre: modern western action. Era: 1870s American West. Camera: 35mm film, handheld, f/2.8. Light: late afternoon golden hour, sun behind the camera. Tempo: FAST multi-shot, hard cuts, real time, NO slow motion. Sound: on, diegetic only. 16:9, 14 seconds.

SCENE CONTEXT — <<<4b3edef4-6f4b-41a5-a67c-9327dabea405>>> and <<<af02fbe9-97af-43c4-919c-a8eb85f59868>>> are FLEEING. They climb the ladder from the gangway onto the roof and RUN along the roofs of two coaches toward the rear of the train, as fast as they can, shooting only the men who get in their way, never stopping. SIX hard-cut shots from different angles over 14 seconds. Photoreal western, no IP.

RULE 1 — ALWAYS FORWARD. From the moment they reach the roof they never stop, never turn back, never stand still, never pose. Every second they are moving toward the rear of the train: sprinting, jumping, ducking on the move. They shoot WHILE RUNNING, without breaking stride, or in a half-second crouch-slide that keeps them going. No dramatic pauses, no looks at each other, no hero beats. They are running for their lives.

RULE 2 — EVERY SHOT HITS AN ENEMY IN FRAME. Nobody ever fires into empty space. Every time a revolver is fired, the gunman being shot is VISIBLE in the same frame, the barrel is pointed at him, and he is hit and falls right after the flash. No enemy falls without being shot; no shot is fired without a visible enemy. Shooter, gun, target, hit — all in one frame, every time.

RULE 3 — REAL SPEED. A flat-out sprint on a moving train: legs driving, arms pumping, coat and dress whipping, boots hammering. NO slow motion, no ramping, no float, no gliding, no dreamy beat anywhere — not even on the jump. If anything looks slow, it is wrong.
